On January 22, 2026, your firm terminated the former Plant Manager due to repeated and ongoing data integrity violations, including, but not limited to, destruction of batch production records, destruction of laboratory-controlled records, and documentation of false production and laboratory data. According to your Quality Head, employees working in the production and laboratory areas were instructed by the former Plant Manager to destroy, alter, or manipulate records and felt compelled to comply due to his supervisory authority. This inadequate practice was also observed and confirmed by your Operations Manager to whom the former Plant Manager reported to. Despite these identified data integrity concerns, your firm did not initiate an investigation or conduct a comprehensive evaluation of manufacturing and laboratory records associated with OTC drug products manufactured for the U.S. market to determine the extent and impact of the data integrity breaches. In addition, your firm did not perform reconciliation of incoming raw materials, finished drug products manufactured and released, inventory records, equipment usage logbooks, laboratory test results, sample collection records, or batch production records to determine whether additional discrepancies or undocumented activities occurred. In addition, your firm did not implement interim controls to prevent recurrence of data integrity failures. The former Plant Manager oversaw production operations from June 2019 through January 2026. Since March 2024, your firm has manufactured 4« lots of OG) intended for the U.S. market, all of which remain within their expiration dates. Moreover, on February 4, 2026, during the initial inspectional walkthrough of your facility, the following data integrity deficiencies were observed: A. Destroyed controlled records containing raw data were observed inside a trash bag located in the scrap room. The recovered documents included, but were not limited to, executed production batch records; media preparation, incubation, and sterilization cycle logbook pages; finished product sample collection forms; environmental monitoring sample forms; and change control log forms. B. The Incubation Usage Log, Book Numbetg Reference SOP: QCD-M/007 & II, containe [redacted] entries (Serial Numbers 4through qq that were signed by the analyst (QC Microbiologist) and verified by a second person (QC Chemist) despite incubation end date not being reported. C. Controlled documents issued by Quality Assurance were not adequately controlled or reconciled. Specifically, your firm did not perform document retrieval as required by logbook (Book Number: [redacted] titled “Formats/Document Issuance & Retrieval Log”, Reference SOP: QAD/004 II, to ensure that all controlled printed copies were returned to Quality Assurance and reconciled. D. The Media Preparation Sterilization and Weight Balance Log, Book Numbetg)4 Reference SOP: QCD-M/001 & I), contained gw media volume entries recorded in pencil rather than permanent ink.
